mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting central bank tightening expectations that depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 5.0%), a further decline in unemployment signals labor market overheating and potential inflation, triggering central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy and tight labor market, jointly driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative policy and tight labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS < 0.25% and UNRATE < 5.5%) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong GDP growth regime (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%), accelerating economic expansion supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth exceeds 2.0%.
